nodes.label: TimeTracker (tray logger)
nodes.rationale: Tray icon background app that logs foreground window changes and idle/active state to CSV files

nodes.label: TimeTrackerDisplay (CSV viewer)
nodes.rationale: WinForms app that reads the CSV files and visualizes them with pie charts and activity timelines

nodes.label: CSV Log File Format
nodes.rationale: CSV used as zero-dependency data exchange format. TimeTracker writes {yyyy-M-d}-app.csv and {yyyy-M-d}-idle.csv to %%LOCALAPPDATA%%\\TimeTracker\. TimeTrackerDisplay reads and parses them with auto-pair discovery.

nodes.label: Idle Detection via Cursor + Keyboard
nodes.rationale: Idle state determined by cumulative cursor movement distance and key press count over a configurable time window (default 3 min). Thresholds stored in app settings: CursorMoveThresholdPixels (2000), KeyInputThreshold (10).

nodes.label: Pie Chart Visualization
nodes.rationale: Uses built-in System.Windows.Forms.DataVisualization.Charting to render two pie charts per day: app usage grouped by application name, and active/idle status breakdown. No NuGet dependencies required.

nodes.label: Auto CSV Pair Discovery
nodes.rationale: CsvParser.DiscoverPairedFiles() regex-matches filenames {date}-app.csv and {date}-idle.csv to auto-include siblings when user selects one file of a pair.

nodes.label: WinForms UI Framework (.NET 4.0)
nodes.rationale: Both projects target .NET Framework 4.0 using WinForms, maximizing compatibility with Visual Studio 2019 and avoiding additional framework dependencies.

nodes.label: Timeline Bar Visualization
nodes.rationale: Custom Panel subclass draws color-coded horizontal timeline: green=active, orange=idle. Second bar shows per-application segments. Hourly tick marks with time labels. Legend in top-left corner.
